title: Mitigating quantum decoherence via global optimal control
authors: Ashkan Abedi, Roberto Menta, Julien Despres, Marco Polini, Francesco Caravelli, Vittorio Giovannetti
abstract: We show that global optimal control can drastically suppress the impact of decoherence in globally driven superconducting quantum computing architectures, taking as a prototype a recently proposed quasi-two-dimensional ladder geometry. Using a tensor-network-based approach, we quantify how amplitude-damping and dephasing channels degrade the flow of quantum information along the ladder and the fidelity of one- and two-qubit gate operations. We then demonstrate that shaping the global drive compresses the gate sequences by an order of magnitude in time, restoring high gate fidelities. We stress that this mitigation is far from trivial: in a globally driven processor, dissipation acts on every physical qubit---including those outside the logical register that sustain the surrounding ordered phases---so its impact cannot be suppressed by protecting an isolated subsystem, and is instead overcome purely through the temporal shaping of the global drive.
summary: The paper investigates how to protect quantum information in large-scale superconducting quantum processors suffering from environmental noise. By applying global optimal control techniques, the authors show that precisely shaping the external driving fields can suppress decoherence effects significantly. This method is crucial because it overcomes dissipation acting across the entire coupled system, not just isolated logical components.
main_problem: The primary goal is mitigating quantum decoherence effects within globally driven superconducting quantum computing architectures.
main_result: Global optimal control can drastically suppress decoherence by temporally shaping the global drive, restoring high gate fidelities even when dissipation acts on all physical qubits.
method: The analysis employs tensor-network-based techniques combined with solving the Lindblad Master Equation (LME) in the rotating frame to simulate dissipative dynamics.
model_or_system: The system is a superconducting qubit array modeled as a quasi-two-dimensional ladder geometry, featuring nearest-neighbor ZZ couplings and global driving fields. The dynamics are governed by an effective Hamiltonian derived from the full time-dependent Hamiltonian.
key_observables: Gate fidelities (1QG, 2QG), quantum information flow degradation, relaxation rate ($\gamma^-$), and dephasing rate ($\gamma_z$).
important_parameters: The dimensionless interaction parameter $\eta = \zeta/\Omega_\chi$, and the decoherence rates $\gamma^-$ and $\gamma_z$.
main_assumptions: Approximations include applying the Rotating-Wave Approximation (RWA) and using a phenomenological Lindblad form for dissipation, assuming zero temperature.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate how gate fidelity decays as a function of relaxation ($\gamma^-$) or dephasing ($\gamma_z$) rates for various operations on the ladder architecture.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the physical model and Hamiltonian, then analyzes decoherence effects using tensor networks to quantify information loss. Finally, it demonstrates that global optimal control over the drive sequence can counteract these losses by compressing gate times.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses hardware limitations in superconducting quantum computing by providing a concrete, physically implementable method (global pulse shaping) to combat decoherence across an entire coupled chip architecture.
